chunks: From him, from Fudayla, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

He was asked about the inlaid sword and the iron sword decorated with silver, whether it is sold for dirhams. He said, 'Sell it for gold.' And he said, 'It is disliked to sell it with deferred payment (nasi'ah).' And he said, 'If the price is more than silver, there is no harm.'
ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic legal rulings on selling decorated weapons like swords?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic preference for selling gold-inlaid swords using gold currency to avoid riba (usury) issues inherent in exchanging unequal weights of the same metal type, while permitting silver if the price exceeds its intrinsic value. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise monetary valuation in commercial transactions to ensure fairness and avoid deferred payment disputes (nasi'ah).
